sources.entry: Cronmaster - Cronjob management UI with human readable syntax, live logging and log history for your cronjobs. AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Cronmaster is a web UI for managing cron jobs and bash scripts on a host, with human-readable scheduling, optional execution logging, and live status updates.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a browser interface to view, create, clone and delete cron jobs, with comments and quick presets for common schedules. Jobs can optionally have execution logging that captures stdout, stderr, exit codes and timestamps, with automatic cleanup. Server-Sent Events stream job status and live log output for long-running jobs when logging is enabled. Users can also create, edit and delete bash scripts in an editor with snippets for use in cron jobs. It shows system information such as uptime, memory, CPU, network and GPU. A REST API with optional API key authentication is available, and login can use password and/or OIDC single sign-on.
use_cases: manage cron jobs through a web interface
schedule recurring bash scripts without editing crontab by hand
view cronjob output and execution history
integrate cron management with external tools via API
protect a cron dashboard with password or SSO login
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml using the minimal example in the README (image ghcr.io/fccview/cronmaster:latest, port 40123:3000, mounts for docker.sock, scripts, data and snippets)
Set AUTH_PASSWORD and HOST_CRONTAB_USER in the environment section
Open the browser at the mapped port
notable: Reads and writes crontab files directly so changes sync in real time with the host's cron
Optional per-job execution logging with live streaming via SSE
Supports both password and OIDC SSO login at the same time
Multi-architecture Docker images for AMD64 and ARM64
caveats: Must run as root in Docker; the README says there is no way around this
Requires mounting the Docker socket and using privileged mode with host PID namespace for the Docker setup
Deleting a script does not remove cron jobs that reference it
keywords: alternative to editing crontab by hand
